texto_aprovado: So why is their venom so deadly to us? A team that studied the toxin thinks it started out as a weapon for catching insects, and that the males turned it into a defense against small animals like bandicoots, birds and lizards. Its lethal effect on humans, in their words, is "an unfortunate evolutionary coincidence." Dogs and cats are insensitive to it.
